questions.question: Comment on nutrient losses during food processing
questions.solution_html:
• Comment on nutrient losses during food processing
  • Nutrient losses during food processing occur due to exposure to heat, light, oxygen, pH changes
  • and mechanical operations. Heat -sensitive vitamins such as vitamin C, thiamine and folate are
  • most vulnerable during thermal processing methods like blanching, boiling and canning. Water -
  • soluble nutrients also leach out into the cooking water when foods are washed, soaked or boiled.
  • Oxidation during cutting, grinding and pro longed storage further reduces the levels of vitamins
  • A, E and certain antioxidants. However, some processing methods such as steaming, minimal
  • processing and vacuum cooking help retain nutrients more effectively. Although some nutrient
  • loss is unavoidable, processing can improve the bioavailability of nutrients in certain foods, such
  • as increasing lycopene availability in cooked tomatoes. Thus, nutrient loss depends on the type
  • and intensity of the processing method used.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Describe the differences between tertiary processing and primary and secondary processing.
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the differences betwe en tertiary processing and pr imary and secondary
  • processing
  • Primary processing involves basic operations that convert raw agricultural materials into forms
  • suitable for consumption or further processing, such as cleaning, sorting, milling, peeling and
  • drying. Secondary processing transforms these primary products into more refined or finished
  • foods, such as baking bread from flour, making cheese from milk or producing jams and sauces.
  • Tertiary processing, however, deals with the creation of highly proce ssed, ready -to-eat or
  • convenience foods designed for immediate consumption. Examples include packaged snacks,
  • instant noodles, ready -to-heat meals, breakfast cereals and frozen dinners. While primary and
  • secondary processing focus on raw material transform ation and product development, tertiary
  • processing emphasizes convenience, extended shelf life, value addition and consumer appeal
  • through advanced food engineering and packaging technologies.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Write a short note on importance of food processing / [CO1, CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Write a short note on the importance of food processing
  • Food processing plays a crucial role in ensuring food safety, improving shelf life and providing
  • convenience to consumers. It helps in destroying harmful microorganisms, preventing spoilage
  • and reducing foodborne illnesses. Processing methods such as pasteur ization, canning, freezing
  • and dehydration allow foods to remain stable for long periods, reducing post -harvest losses. It
  • also improves the digestibility, palatability and nutritional value of foods through controlled
  • heating, fermentation and fortificati on. Furthermore, processing creates a wide variety of food
  • products that cater to diverse dietary needs, such as low -fat, fortified, gluten-free or ready-to-eat
  • foods. By enhancing market value, reducing wastage and enabling year -round availability of
  • seasonal products, food processing becomes an essential part of modern food systems.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of drying as a food preservation method.
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of drying as a food preservation method
  • Drying offers several advantages in food preservation. It significantly reduces the moist ure
  • content, which prevents the growth of bacteria, yeasts and molds. This extends shelf life and
  • reduces the need for refrigeration. Dried foods are lightweight, easy to store and convenient for
  • transport. Drying also retains many nutrients compared to se vere heat treatments. However,
  • drying has some disadvantages. Heat -sensitive vitamins like vitamin C and B -complex can be
  • lost during drying. Some drying methods may cause shrinkage, texture changes and loss of
  • natural flavor. Improper drying or storage ma y lead to moisture absorption and spoilage.
  • Additionally, certain traditional drying methods depend heavily on weather and may not ensure
  • uniform drying. Despite limitations, drying remains an economical and effective preservation
  • technique.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Give a detailed note on dehydration with its principle. / [CO1, CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Give a detailed note on dehydration with its principle
  • Dehydration is a food preservation technique that involves removing moisture from food to
  • inhibit microbial growth and enzymatic activity. The principle of dehydration is based on
  • reducing water activity (aw), thereby preventing microorganisms from multiplying. In
  • dehydration, heat is applied under controlled conditions to evaporate water from the food
  • surface, while air circulation carries the moisture away. Modern dehydration methods include
  • tray drying, spray drying, drum drying, freeze drying and tunnel drying. Dehydrated foods
  • become lighter, shelf -stable and easy to store and transport. The process must be carefully
  • controlled to prevent case hardening, nutritional loss and undesirable texture changes. By
  • maintaining optimal temperature, airflow and humidity, dehydration preserves the nutritional
  • quality, color and flavor of foods more effectively.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Exaplain canning of fruits [4x5 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain canning of fruits
  • Canning of fruits is a heat -based preservation method in which fruits are proces sed and sealed in
  • airtight containers to prevent spoilage. First, fresh fruits are washed, peeled, trimmed and cut as
  • required. They are then filled into cans or jars along with syrup, juice or water to improve flavor
  • and texture. The filled containers are exhausted to remove trapped air, which helps create a
  • vacuum seal. Next, the cans are sealed and subjected to heat treatment at appropriate
  • temperatures to destroy spoilage organisms and enzymes. Since fruits are high -acid foods, they
  • can be safely proces sed at around 100°C in a water bath. After heating, the cans are rapidly
  • cooled to prevent overcooking and ensure product stability. Proper canning maintains the color,
  • flavor and nutritional quality of fruits while extending shelf life for months or years.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
